verdicts.argument: Checked both 10-Ks myself. The FY2024 sentence 'The effect of reducing prices and reimbursement for certain of our products would significantly impact our results of operations' is on ABBV:10k_FY2024.md p.36 and has no match anywhere in ABBV:10k_FY2025.md. The 340B admission ('growth in entities claiming entitlement to 340B pricing has increased the portion of our sales subject to such discounts') is new on ABBV:10k_FY2025.md p.23; the FY2024 equivalent (p.21) lists 340B only as a law. A peer search of annual reports for the same 340B-share wording found no shortlist match, so it is not boilerplate every company carries. Calls: 340B was raised only in passing by Rob Michael on the 2025Q1 call (grade C, ABBV:companies/ABBV/transcripts/2025Q1_transcript.md p.16) as a lobbying priority, not as a growing share of sales; market/never_asked.csv#3 shows MFN asked in 1 of 10 quarters (last 2025Q1). Weakening points: the MFN deal and its Medicaid/TrumpRx terms are a press-release headline (ABBV:policy/press_2026-01-12_mfn_trump_agreement.md p.1), so the 'MFN spillover' half of the claim is the obvious consequence of a headline, and 340B is now itself a headline: on 2026-10-02 AbbVie press-released joining the HRSA 340B Rebate Model Pilot for Imbruvica, Linzess and Vraylar from 2027 (ABBV:policy/press_2026-10-02_340b_rebate_pilot.md p.1). Neither release states that the 340B share of sales has grown, and no call says the 'would significantly impact' sentence was dropped.
verdicts.correction: Drop the MFN-spillover half (it restates the January 2026 press release). Keep the narrow drift: the 'would significantly impact' sentence deleted (10-K FY2024 p.36 vs FY2025) plus the new 340B-share admission (10-K FY2025 p.23). Strengthen it by linking it to the 2026-10-02 340B rebate-pilot release, which names the same three IRA drugs; the release frames the pilot as integrity policy, but the 10-K says 340B is eating a rising share of sales.

verdicts.argument: The main driver of the rebate step-up was guided in dollars, product by product, on the 2024Q4 call (grade C, ABBV:companies/ABBV/transcripts/2024Q4_transcript.md p.8-9): 2025 revenue 'despite a roughly 4% net unfavorable impact across our portfolio from the Medicare Part D benefit redesign', with $600M for Humira, $400M for Imbruvica, $100M for Venclexta and $200M for Vraylar. Steve Scala (TD Cowen) asked about it directly (p.18). Scott Reents explained that the headwind had moved from 3% to 4% on mix, and Rob Michael put it at 'approximately $2 billion'. Part D redesign also came up in the 2024Q1 and 2024Q2 calls (pages 10, 18; page 9). market/priced_in_scorecard.csv#5 and never_asked.csv#5 show gross-to-net/price asked in 8 of 10 quarters (12 analyst turns, last asked 2026Q2), so this is one of the most-asked AbbVie topics. Consensus already reflects it: market/consensus_vs_guidance.csv#2 has 2026 revenue consensus of $67,618M against guidance of $67,600M. The 34% provision jump in the 10-K FY2025 p.49 roll-forward is the accounting footprint of a pre-announced, sized headwind. The BMY contrast mostly reflects AbbVie's heavier Part D mix, which management said plainly ('high Part D channel mix').
verdicts.correction: The only part that might not be obvious is the residual: the provision rose about $5.4B while management guided about $2B net. That leaves roughly $3B that the guided Part D effect does not explain, though gross versus net accounting may close much of it. It survives only if the reader can show the excess is Medicaid mix (Humira biosimilar shift, the MFN Medicaid commitment) rather than the guided Part D redesign.

verdicts.argument: No call or release sizes a year-end 2025 build. The 2025Q4 transcript (grade C, ABBV:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1) has no hit for inventory, stocking, wholesaler or destock. The 2026Q2 transcript (grade D) has none either. market/never_asked.csv#7 shows inventory/channel last asked in 2025Q1 (an unasked streak of 5 quarters), so the market is not watching it. Partly pre-empting it: on the 2026Q1 call (grade C, p.1) Scott Reents said plainly 'There was a slight amount of inventory destock as well' for Skyrizi, which acknowledges an unwind. AbbVie also discussed channel inventory in 2024Q1 (calls/qa_turns.csv#11, about $50M for Juvederm and Botox). Not obvious, but the company has already half-explained the unwind, and this lens cannot rescue its low materiality.
verdicts.correction: Frame it as: the year-end 2025 receivables and finished-goods build was never sized, and management mentioned only a 'slight' Skyrizi destock in Q1 2026. Do not claim nobody mentioned inventory.

verdicts.argument: Confirmed silent. The Q4 2025 earnings release still breaks out Eye Care at $2,109M with Ozurdex 493 and Alphagan/Combigan 197 (ABBV:earnings/2026-02-04_abbv-20251231xexhibit991.md p.6-7). The Q1 2026 release product table (ABBV:earnings/2026-04-29_abbv-20260331xexhibit991.md p.6) runs Aesthetics straight to 'Other Key Products' with no Eye Care rows and carries no reclassification note. Neither 2026 10-Q (ABBV:10q_2026Q1.md, ABBV:10q_2026Q2.md) mentions 'eye' on any page. The April 2026 8-K (ABBV:earnings/2026-04-03_abbv-20260403.md) gives no recast. On calls, eye care was last discussed in 2024Q3 and 2024Q4 (grade C, a Geoff Meacham question and 2025 guidance of $2.2B on 2024Q4 p.9). 'Eye care', 'Ozurdex' and 'glaucoma' get zero hits in the 2025Q4, 2026Q1 and 2026Q2 transcripts. The only headline touching it is the TrumpRx listing of Alphagan/Combigan in the MFN press release, which says nothing about reporting. Not starter thread, not a patent cliff.

Much of the claim is plainly stated. The Skyrizi royalty is given in dollars on nearly every call: 'nearly $2.2 billion of SKYRIZI royalty payments' (2025Q3, grade B, Scott Reents) and 'roughly $3.5 billion of SKYRIZI royalty payments' in 2026 guidance (2025Q4, grade C). An analyst asked about it as early as 2024Q1 (p.23-24). The fair-value charge appears as a reconciling line in every earnings release (for example 'Change in fair value of contingent consideration 3,905' in ABBV:earnings/2026-07-31_abbv-20260630xexhibit991.md p.12). The 'past the 2033 patent' angle is also partly said: on the 2026Q1 call (grade C, p.1) Rob Michael answered a direct LOE question that Skyrizi has 'later expiring IP ... patents expiring in the U.S. in the mid-2030s and later'. A royalty horizon of 2037 therefore matches management's public exclusivity view. The 10-K FY2025 p.83 shows the horizon moved from 2034 to 2037, and the 10-Q 2026Q1 p.14 already showed 2026-2037. What is not said anywhere: the 2044 tail and the 38% probability for 'pipeline assets in combination with Skyrizi'. They appear only in ABBV:10q_2026Q2.md p.15 and p.33, not in the 10-Q 2026Q1, and get no hit in any transcript, release or 8-K for '2044', 'contingent' or 'combination ... royalty'. Meanwhile management calls the Skyrizi-backbone combination strategy 'underappreciated' (2025Q3, grade B, Robert A. Michael). This is the least obvious item in the ABBV set.
verdicts.correction: Narrow the claim to the new combination-asset royalty tail. As of the June 2026 10-Q, the partner royalty also attaches to pipeline combinations with Skyrizi through 2044 (38% probability), while management pitches those combinations as its next immunology leg. Drop the 'lengthened to 2037, four years past the patent' framing as the headline: management has publicly said Skyrizi IP runs to the mid-2030s and later, and the royalty size is a recurring call disclosure.

verdicts.argument: Medicare negotiation is one of the case's three named forces, and the percentage cuts are headline numbers on the CMS fact sheets. The Imbruvica effect is stated plainly in prepared remarks on the 2025Q4 call (grade C, ABBV:transcripts/2025Q4_transcript.md p.1): 2026 growth 'despite headwinds from continued HUMIRA erosion and IMBRUVICA IRA pricing' and 'we do anticipate IMBRUVICA IRA price pricing will unfavorably impact our oncology portfolio growth in 2026'. The Vraylar and Linzess question was asked by two analysts on the 2025Q3 call (grade B), and IRA negotiation was asked in 4 of 10 quarters (market/priced_in_scorecard.csv#2). Management's answer, that the outcomes 'will not impact our long-term guidance', is itself on the record, and 2026 consensus sits on guidance (market/consensus_vs_guidance.csv#2). The scaling arithmetic (CMS cut times U.S. sales) is what any analyst does with a public fact sheet. The Imbruvica comparison also mixes in BTK competition, which management names as the primary cause of the decline ('primarily due to continued competitive dynamics', 2025Q4 p.1).
verdicts.correction: This would become non-obvious only with drug-level Medicare share data showing Vraylar or Linzess exposure larger than a naive cut-times-U.S.-sales estimate implies, or with 2027 consensus that has not moved for the November 2025 prices. Neither is in hand (no partd rows for Vraylar or Linzess). As written it restates the IRA force.

verdicts.argument: Every element is said plainly. Chris Schott (JPMorgan) raised 'the TREMFYA subcu induction dosing kind of rolling out' on the 2025Q3 call (grade B), and Roopal Thakkar answered with Skyrizi's own SC induction plan. The Crohn's-only SC filing is an earnings-release headline: 'seeking approval for Skyrizi (risankizumab) for subcutaneous (SC) induction in ... Crohn's disease (CD)' (ABBV:earnings/2026-04-29_abbv-20260331xexhibit991.md p.3). The UC gap was stated in prepared remarks on the 2026Q1 call (grade C, p.1): 'Subcu induction for ulcerative colitis is also being assessed and we will be discussing options with health authorities.' An analyst on the same call linked Skyrizi pricing to 'IBD and IV induction'. The 2026Q2 call (grade D) repeats the Crohn's-only filing with a fall decision. Liver testing at IBD initiation was also asked about on the 2024Q3 call (grade C, p.11). The only unsaid detail is that Skyrizi's hepatotoxicity case occurred after two labeled 600 mg IV doses (drug:skyrizi:label_sections.md p.19), which is a label nuance, not this candidate's claim.
verdicts.correction: Drop as a finding. If kept for the product comparison, lead with the label-text hepatotoxicity contrast (Skyrizi's case at the labeled IV dose versus Tremfya's at a higher-than-labeled dose) rather than IV-versus-SC induction, which management and analysts have discussed for a year.

verdicts.argument: The U.S. concentration was put to the CEO in exactly these terms by Courtney Breen (Bernstein) on the 2025Q3 call (grade B, p.1): 'about a 75% US exposure, versus 25% ex-US'. Robert A. Michael answered on the record, giving the 75/25 split and the pre-Humira two-thirds/one-third history. It is also the geography table in every 10-K (10-K FY2025 p.41). The $100B pledge, the tariff and price-mandate exemption and the Medicaid terms are the headline bullets of the MFN press release (ABBV:policy/press_2026-01-12_mfn_trump_agreement.md p.1) and were repeated in 2025Q4 prepared remarks (grade C, p.1). The 'pledge is business-as-usual spend' inference is not stated, but by construction it applies to every shortlist signatory's R&D-plus-capex, so it does not distinguish AbbVie. The per-1% U.S. price sensitivity is generic MFN arithmetic built on the case's own force.
verdicts.correction: This would become non-obvious only if a peer's pledge were shown to be clearly incremental to its run-rate while AbbVie's was not. That needs peer R&D-plus-capex lines, not the compiled force table. Otherwise fold the 76% U.S. share into context, not findings.

verdicts.argument: Skyrizi is the starter-thread product itself: the case appendix frames AbbVie as 'Life after Humira: how fast Skyrizi and Rinvoq are filling the revenue gap' (docs/case/fine_print_case.pdf p.5). Every AbbVie team will pick it, which is acceptable for the product slot. The stated fine_print_edge, however, is the IV-only induction versus Tremfya SC, and it is plainly on the record. It was raised on the 2025Q3 call (grade B, Chris Schott), the Crohn's SC filing is in the Q1 2026 earnings release (p.3), and the UC gap was stated in 2026Q1 prepared remarks (grade C). The Part B ASP versus NADAC point cites unverified pricing rows (fact:pricing/gtn_exposure.csv#21) and was not checked here.
verdicts.correction: Keep Skyrizi, but rebuild the edge around items not yet said publicly: (1) the hepatotoxicity case at the labeled 600 mg IV dose (drug:skyrizi:label_sections.md p.19) versus Tremfya's at a higher-than-labeled dose; (2) tie it to the financial finding ABBV-c05, where the 2044 combination-royalty tail means Skyrizi's 'backbone' combinations carry the partner royalty. That connection is not on any call.

overall: AbbVie's material is mostly well covered: Part D redesign, IRA cuts, U.S. concentration, the MFN pledge and Skyrizi's IV-versus-SC induction were all quantified or discussed on calls or in press releases, so c02, c06, c07 and c08 add little beyond the starter thread and the case's own three forces. What survives is in filings that nobody has discussed. The best of it is the June 2026 10-Q's 2044 Skyrizi-combination royalty tail (c05, narrowed), followed by the silent Eye Care fold into 'All other' (c04) and the 340B-share admission in the 10-K (c01, narrowed).
